encounter_context: outpatient oncology clinic visit during active chemotherapy treatment for right breast cancer
allowed_distractors: chemotherapy-related fatigue and nausea, expected side effects being managed
history of benign fibrocystic changes in left breast, years ago, fully resolved
trap_patterns: CRITICAL: the primary tumor is in the RIGHT breast — do not reference the left breast as the malignant site
both the malignant neoplasm and the chemotherapy encounter must be addressed in the assessment and plan
do not describe completed treatment, remission, or surgery as the focus — the patient is in active chemotherapy treatment
do not imply specific chemotherapy agents unless the encounter context clearly supports naming them

active_conditions: personal history of malignant neoplasm of sigmoid colon
encounter_context: outpatient gastroenterology or surgical oncology surveillance visit after curative sigmoid colectomy for colorectal cancer
allowed_distractors: mild post-surgical adhesion-related discomfort, chronic and stable
history of prior adenomatous polyps on earlier colonoscopy, relevant surveillance context
trap_patterns: CRITICAL: this is PERSONAL HISTORY (post-curative treatment surveillance) — the cancer is NOT currently active; describe a monitoring visit, not active cancer treatment
surveillance activities should be the clinical focus: CEA levels, colonoscopy intervals, imaging follow-up
do not describe active cancer recurrence unless explicitly seeded as an active condition
do not imply the patient is currently receiving chemotherapy or radiation therapy

active_conditions: malignant neoplasm of upper lobe, right bronchus and lung
encounter_context: pulmonology or thoracic oncology clinic for new or early-stage lung malignancy evaluation and treatment planning
allowed_distractors: extensive history of tobacco smoking, the primary identified risk factor
chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, a background respiratory comorbidity
trap_patterns: CRITICAL: the tumor is in the UPPER LOBE of the RIGHT lung — do not reference the left lung or right lower lobe as the primary tumor site
this is a new diagnosis or early treatment phase encounter — do not describe completed treatment or remission
imaging findings such as CT chest or PET scan are appropriate to include
do not specify histological subtype such as adenocarcinoma or squamous cell unless the encounter context specifically supports naming it

active_conditions: malignant neoplasm of prostate, on active surveillance
encounter_context: urology clinic follow-up for low-risk or very-low-risk prostate cancer being managed with active surveillance rather than immediate treatment
allowed_distractors: co-existing benign prostatic hyperplasia managed separately
mild lower urinary tract symptoms including frequency and nocturia, potentially related to BPH
trap_patterns: CRITICAL: the patient is on ACTIVE SURVEILLANCE — the cancer is diagnosed but treatment is being intentionally deferred; do not describe active treatment such as radiation, prostatectomy, or hormone therapy unless seeded
PSA trend and biopsy surveillance schedule should be referenced as part of the monitoring narrative
do not imply high-risk or metastatic prostate cancer — the encounter context is low-risk active surveillance
do not confuse active surveillance with watchful waiting — active surveillance includes scheduled repeat biopsies and PSA monitoring

active_conditions: personal history of malignant neoplasm of right breast
lymphedema following mastectomy of right breast
encounter_context: outpatient oncology or lymphedema clinic follow-up after completed breast cancer treatment with persistent right arm lymphedema
allowed_distractors: mild osteopenia related to prior hormone therapy, background finding
history of sentinel lymph node biopsy as part of original staging, completed
trap_patterns: CRITICAL: laterality must be RIGHT throughout — the mastectomy and the lymphedema are on the RIGHT side
personal history means the breast cancer itself is treated and resolved — do not imply active breast cancer recurrence
lymphedema is the PRIMARY ACTIVE clinical problem in this visit — it must be well-evidenced with right arm swelling, heaviness, skin changes, circumferential measurements, or compression garment use
do not imply left-arm or bilateral lymphedema unless explicitly seeded

allowed_distractors: treatment-related fatigue, residual but gradually improving
history of grade 2 to 3 neutropenia during prior chemotherapy, now fully recovered

the note must read as a monitoring visit, not active treatment — describe routine surveillance labs, imaging intervals, and follow-up planning
do not imply disease relapse or progression unless explicitly seeded as an active condition
do not specify lymphoma subtype such as diffuse large B-cell or follicular unless the encounter context specifically supports that level of detail

active_conditions: malignant melanoma of skin of right upper limb, including shoulder
encounter_context: dermatology or surgical oncology clinic visit for melanoma evaluation and initial treatment planning
allowed_distractors: history of prior atypical or dysplastic nevi removed at prior visits
history of significant cumulative sun exposure and sunburn history

do not imply metastatic disease or distant spread unless explicitly seeded

do not describe chemotherapy as the primary treatment — surgery with wide local excision plus sentinel node biopsy and immunotherapy or targeted therapy are more typical initial management for melanoma

encounter_context: outpatient oncology clinic for management of metastatic colorectal cancer with liver involvement
allowed_distractors: history of prior sigmoid colectomy representing the original colorectal cancer resection
treatment-related side effects from prior or current chemotherapy regimens

do not imply that the liver tumor is a primary hepatocellular carcinoma — it is a metastasis from the colorectal primary
imaging findings such as CT abdomen or PET scan showing liver lesions in the context of colorectal cancer are appropriate to include
